\chapter{Learning Theory — Convex Minimax No Regret}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.Minimax.ConvexMinimaxNoRegret
\section{Overview}

This module formalises the no-regret proof route for the convex-compact minimax theorem
(Cesa-Bianchi--Lugosi Theorem~7.1).  Starting from a finite-row sample lower value and
the finite minimax theorem, it assembles three ingredients---a finite no-regret bound, a
compact approximation step, and uniform equicontinuity---to establish the full minimax
equality $\inf_{x \in X} \sup_{y \in Y} f(x,y) = \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in X} f(x,y)$
under convexity, concavity, and compactness hypotheses.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Finite row sample lower value]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finiteRowSampleLowerValue}
\label{OnlineLearning.finiteRowSampleLowerValue}
\leanok
Given a payoff $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and a finite subset
$u \subseteq X$, the \emph{finite row sample lower value} is
\[
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in u} f(x, y),
\]
i.e.\ the lower value obtained when the row player is restricted to the finite sample $u$
while the column player still ranges over all of $Y$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finite no-regret bound predicate]
\lean{OnlineLearning.Theorem71FiniteNoRegretBound}
\label{OnlineLearning.Theorem71FiniteNoRegretBound}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.finiteRowSampleLowerValue}
$\texttt{OnlineLearning.Theorem71FiniteNoRegretBound}$ is the proposition asserting that
for every nonempty finite row sample $u \subseteq X$,
\[
  \inf_{x \in X} \sup_{y \in Y} f(x,y)
    \;\le\;
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in u} f(x, y).
\]
This is the finite-game no-regret ingredient in the Theorem~7.1 proof route.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Compact approximation predicate]
\lean{OnlineLearning.Theorem71CompactApproximation}
\label{OnlineLearning.Theorem71CompactApproximation}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.finiteRowSampleLowerValue}
$\texttt{OnlineLearning.Theorem71CompactApproximation}$ is the proposition asserting that
for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a nonempty finite sample $u \subseteq X$ such
that
\[
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in u} f(x, y)
    \;\le\;
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in X} f(x, y) + \varepsilon.
\]
This encodes the ``let the net size go to zero'' compactness step of the textbook proof.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Uniform equicontinuity in the row variable]
\lean{OnlineLearning.Theorem71UniformEquicontinuity}
\label{OnlineLearning.Theorem71UniformEquicontinuity}
\leanok
$\texttt{OnlineLearning.Theorem71UniformEquicontinuity}$ holds for $X$, $Y$, $f$ when $f$
is uniformly equicontinuous in its first argument uniformly over all columns: for every
$\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $\rho > 0$ such that for all $x, x' \in X$ and $y \in Y$,
\[
  \dist(x, x') < \rho \;\Longrightarrow\; |f(x,y) - f(x',y)| < \varepsilon.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finite indexed row sample lower value]
\lean{OnlineLearning.finiteIndexedRowSampleLowerValue}
\label{OnlineLearning.finiteIndexedRowSampleLowerValue}
\leanok
For a row sample indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}\,M$, the \emph{finite indexed row sample lower
value} is
\[
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,M} f(x_i, y),
\]
where $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,M \to X$ is the sample.  This is a technical variant of
$\texttt{OnlineLearning.finiteRowSampleLowerValue}$ used in intermediate results.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Minimax equality on convex compact sets]
\lean{OnlineLearning.convex_compact_minimax_of_theorem71_route}
\label{OnlineLearning.convex_compact_minimax_of_theorem71_route}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses, OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxStatement, OnlineLearning.Theorem71CompactApproximation, OnlineLearning.Theorem71FiniteNoRegretBound, OnlineLearning.weak_convex_compact_minimax}
\difficulty{3}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ and let $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$. Suppose that $X$ and $Y$
are nonempty, that $X$ is compact and convex, that $Y$ is convex, that the map $x
\mapsto f(x,y)$ is continuous and convex on $X$ for every $y \in Y$, that the map $y
\mapsto f(x,y)$ is concave on $Y$ for every $x \in X$, and that $f$ is bounded above and
below on $X \times Y$. Suppose moreover that for every nonempty finite subset $u
\subseteq X$,
\[
  \inf_{x \in X} \sup_{y \in Y} f(x,y) \;\le\; \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in u} f(x,y),
\]
and that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a nonempty finite subset $u \subseteq
X$ with
\[
\sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in u} f(x,y) \;\le\; \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in X} f(x,y) +
\varepsilon.
\]
Then
\[
  \inf_{x \in X} \sup_{y \in Y} f(x,y) \;=\; \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in X} f(x,y).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Compact approximation of the lower value from uniform equicontinuity]
\lean{OnlineLearning.theorem71_compactApproximation_of_uniformEquicontinuity}
\label{OnlineLearning.theorem71_compactApproximation_of_uniformEquicontinuity}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses, OnlineLearning.Theorem71CompactApproximation, OnlineLearning.Theorem71UniformEquicontinuity, OnlineLearning.finiteRowSampleLowerValue}
\difficulty{5}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ be nonempty, with $X$ compact and convex and $Y$ convex, and
let $f : \bbr \times \bbr \to \bbr$ be bounded above and below on $X \times Y$, with
$f(\cdot, y)$ continuous and convex on $X$ for every $y \in Y$ and $f(x, \cdot)$ concave
on $Y$ for every $x \in X$. Suppose in addition that $f$ is uniformly equicontinuous in
its first argument, uniformly over the columns: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is
$\rho > 0$ with $|f(x,y) - f(x',y)| < \varepsilon$ whenever $x, x' \in X$, $y \in Y$,
and $\dist(x, x') < \rho$. Then for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists a nonempty
finite sample $u \subseteq X$ such that
\[
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in u} f(x, y)
    \;\le\;
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in X} f(x, y) + \varepsilon;
\]
that is, restricting the row player to a suitable finite subset of $X$ raises the lower
value of the game by at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform equicontinuity in the row variable from joint continuity on a compact domain]
\lean{OnlineLearning.theorem71_uniformEquicontinuity_of_jointContinuous_compact}
\label{OnlineLearning.theorem71_uniformEquicontinuity_of_jointContinuous_compact}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses, OnlineLearning.Theorem71UniformEquicontinuity}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ and $f : \bbr \times \bbr \to \bbr$ satisfy the convex-compact
minimax hypotheses, and suppose in addition that $Y$ is compact and that $(x,y) \mapsto
f(x,y)$ is continuous on $X \times Y$. Then $f$ is uniformly equicontinuous in its first
argument, uniformly over all columns: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $\rho >
0$ such that for all $x, x' \in X$ and all $y \in Y$,
\[
  \dist(x, x') < \rho \;\Longrightarrow\; |f(x,y) - f(x',y)| < \varepsilon.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Compact approximation from joint continuity on a compact column set]
\lean{OnlineLearning.theorem71_compactApproximation_of_jointContinuous_compact}
\label{OnlineLearning.theorem71_compactApproximation_of_jointContinuous_compact}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses, OnlineLearning.Theorem71CompactApproximation, OnlineLearning.theorem71_compactApproximation_of_uniformEquicontinuity, OnlineLearning.theorem71_uniformEquicontinuity_of_jointContinuous_compact}
\difficulty{1}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ and $f : \bbr \times \bbr \to \bbr$ satisfy the convex-compact
minimax hypotheses, and suppose in addition that $Y$ is compact and that $f$ is jointly
continuous on $X \times Y$. Then for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a nonempty finite
subset $u \subseteq X$ such that
\[
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in u} f(x,y)
    \;\le\;
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in X} f(x,y) + \varepsilon;
\]
that is, restricting the row player to a suitable finite sample raises the lower value
by at most $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Upper minimax value bounded by a finite row sample's lower value]
\lean{OnlineLearning.theorem71_finiteIndexedNoRegretBound_normalized}
\label{OnlineLearning.theorem71_finiteIndexedNoRegretBound_normalized}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses, OnlineLearning.exists_forall_le_of_finite_sublevel_intersections, OnlineLearning.finiteIndexedRowSampleLowerValue, OnlineLearning.finiteLowerValue, OnlineLearning.finiteUpperValue, OnlineLearning.finite_minimax_value, OnlineLearning.minimaxSublevel, OnlineLearning.payoffVsPure_nonneg, OnlineLearning.pureVsPayoff_le_one, ZeroSumGame, payoffVsPure, pureVsPayoff}
\difficulty{7}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ satisfy the convex-compact minimax hypotheses for a payoff $f
: \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$, and suppose in addition that $f$ is normalized, $0 \le f(x,y)
\le 1$ for all $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$. Fix an integer $M \ge 2$ and a finite row sample
$x : \mathrm{Fin}\,M \to X$, writing $x_i$ for its $i$-th point. Then
\[
  \inf_{x' \in X}\; \sup_{y \in Y}\; f(x', y)
    \;\le\;
  \sup_{y \in Y}\; \inf_{i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,M}\; f(x_i, y).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite no-regret bound for normalized convex-compact games]
\lean{OnlineLearning.theorem71_finiteNoRegretBound_normalized}
\label{OnlineLearning.theorem71_finiteNoRegretBound_normalized}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses, OnlineLearning.Theorem71FiniteNoRegretBound, OnlineLearning.finiteIndexedRowSampleLowerValue, OnlineLearning.finiteRowSampleLowerValue, OnlineLearning.theorem71_finiteIndexedNoRegretBound_normalized}
\difficulty{5}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ and $f : \bbr \to \bbr \to \bbr$ satisfy the convex-compact
minimax hypotheses, and suppose the payoff is normalized so that $0 \le f(x,y) \le 1$
for all $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$. Then for every nonempty finite subset $u \subseteq X$,
\[
  \inf_{x \in X} \sup_{y \in Y} f(x,y)
    \;\le\;
  \sup_{y \in Y} \inf_{x \in u} f(x,y);
\]
that is, the game's upper value is bounded above by the lower value of the game in which
the row player is restricted to the finite sample $u$ while the column player still
ranges over all of $Y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A normalized convex–concave minimax equality]
\lean{OnlineLearning.convex_compact_minimax_noRegret_jointCompact_normalized}
\label{OnlineLearning.convex_compact_minimax_noRegret_jointCompact_normalized}
\leanok
\uses{OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxHypotheses, OnlineLearning.ConvexCompactMinimaxStatement, OnlineLearning.convex_compact_minimax_of_theorem71_route, OnlineLearning.theorem71_compactApproximation_of_jointContinuous_compact, OnlineLearning.theorem71_finiteNoRegretBound_normalized}
\difficulty{1}
Let $X, Y \subseteq \bbr$ be nonempty, compact, convex sets, and let $f : \bbr \times
\bbr \to \bbr$ be jointly continuous on $X \times Y$ and normalized so that $0 \le
f(x,y) \le 1$ for all $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$. Suppose that $f$ is bounded above and
below on $X \times Y$, that for every $y \in Y$ the map $x \mapsto f(x,y)$ is continuous
and convex on $X$, and that for every $x \in X$ the map $y \mapsto f(x,y)$ is concave on
$Y$. Then
\[
  \inf_{x \in X}\,\sup_{y \in Y}\,f(x,y)
  \;=\;
  \sup_{y \in Y}\,\inf_{x \in X}\,f(x,y).
\]
\end{theorem}
